section_summary.extract_value: This discussion reports that the BSRS (Breast Size Rating Scale) has adequate convergent validity and 15-day test-retest reliability in a sample of Brazilian university women, with breast size ratings correlating moderately with bra band size and breast-size dissatisfaction correlating with BMI and body-image measures. The authors note that a majority of participants were dissatisfied with their breast size (79.4%), and 65.5% desired larger breasts, and they list limitations including a single-region university sample, lack of discriminant/predictive validity testing, and absence of data on breast-modifying procedures.
section_summary.evidence_source: "This is the first study to examine the psychometric properties of BSRS scores in non-British women." "BSRS-derived scores have adequate convergent validity in Brazilian university women... ratings of current breast size were significantly correlated with actual bra size." "BSRS-derived scores retain their test-retest reliability over a 15-day period." "The results of the present study indicated that a majority of participants (79.4% were dissatisfied with their current breast size, with a clear majority (65.5%) desiring larger breasts than they currently had." "First, the study was conducted with university women from a single region in Brazil..."
